title: Erdős Problem #7: Odd Covering Systems
description: Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are odd? Also known as the Erdős-Selfridge Conjecture. OPEN with significant partial results.

overview.historicalContext:
Erdős Problem #7, also known as the Erdős-Selfridge Conjecture, asks whether there exists a covering system whose moduli are all odd. A covering system is a finite collection of congruence classes {aᵢ mod mᵢ} such that every integer belongs to at least one class. The simplest covering system uses moduli {2, 3, 4, 6, 12}, and all known constructions require at least one even modulus.

Significant partial results have been obtained. Hough and Nielsen (2019) proved that every covering system must contain at least one modulus divisible by 2 or 3, meaning an odd covering would necessarily include moduli divisible by 3. Balister, Bollobas, Morris, Sahasrabudhe, and Tiba (2022) proved the stronger result that no covering system exists with all moduli both odd and squarefree, ruling out a natural class of potential counterexamples.

The problem carries prizes from both Erdős ($25 for proving no odd covering exists) and Selfridge ($2000 specifically for an explicit construction). The LCM of any hypothetical odd covering must be divisible by 9 or 15, further constraining what such a system could look like. Despite these restrictions, the general conjecture remains open.
overview.problemStatement: Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are odd? Equivalently, must every covering system have at least one even modulus?

overview.proofStrategy: The formalization defines covering systems via CongruenceClass and CoveringSystem structures, with toSet mapping classes to sets of integers via modular arithmetic. The Erdős-Selfridge conjecture is stated in two equivalent forms. Key partial results are axiomatized: Hough-Nielsen (divisibility by 2 or 3), Balister et al. (no odd squarefree coverings), and LCM constraints.
keyInsights: Conjecture: NO odd covering system exists
Hough-Nielsen (2019): At least one modulus must be divisible by 2 or 3
Balister et al. (2022): No covering exists with all moduli odd AND squarefree
LCM constraint: If an odd covering exists, its LCM must be divisible by 9 or 15
Selfridge offered $2000 for an explicit construction (separate from Erdős's $25)

sections.title: Basic Definitions
sections.mathContext: A covering system $\{a_i \pmod{n_i}\}_{i=1}^k$ covers $\mathbb{Z}$: $\forall x \in \mathbb{Z},\, \exists i: x \equiv a_i \pmod{n_i}$, with distinct $n_i \geq 2$.

sections.title: Odd Moduli
sections.summary: Predicates for odd and even moduli
sections.mathContext: All moduli odd: $2 \nmid n_i$ for all $i$. The Erdős-Selfridge conjecture: no such covering exists.

sections.title: The Erdős-Selfridge Conjecture
sections.summary: Main conjecture in two equivalent forms
sections.mathContext: Conjecture: $\nexists$ covering with all $n_i$ odd and distinct. Equivalently: every covering uses some even modulus.

sections.title: Squarefree Moduli
sections.mathContext: Squarefree: $\forall p$ prime, $p^2 \nmid n_i$. Combined with odd: all moduli are odd squarefree integers.

sections.title: Balister et al. (2022)
sections.mathContext: Balister et al. (2022): $\nexists$ odd squarefree covering system — proved for the squarefree case.

sections.title: Hough-Nielsen (2019)
sections.summary: Some modulus must be divisible by 2 or 3
sections.mathContext: Hough-Nielsen (2019): in any covering, $\exists n_i$ with $2 \mid n_i$ or $3 \mid n_i$. Any odd covering must use a multiple of 3.

sections.title: LCM Constraint
sections.summary: If odd covering exists, LCM divisible by 9 or 15

sections.title: Simple Properties
sections.mathContext: Basic: if all $n_i$ odd, smallest $n_i \geq 3$. Reciprocal sum: $\sum 1/n_i \geq 1$ (covering condition).

sections.title: The Gap
sections.summary: Summary of what is known vs unknown
sections.mathContext: Known: no odd squarefree covering; any covering needs modulus divisible by 2 or 3. Open: odd non-squarefree coverings.

sections.title: Selfridge's Prize
sections.mathContext: Selfridge prize: $2000 for explicit construction of a covering with all $n_i$ odd and distinct (if one exists).

sections.title: Covering with Specific Properties
sections.mathContext: $m^*(\mathcal{C}) = \min\{n_i : n_i \text{ odd}\}$; bounds on the smallest modulus of any hypothetical odd covering.

sections.title: Summary
sections.summary: erdos_7_summary combining Hough-Nielsen, Balister, and LCM constraint
sections.mathContext: Main theorem: Hough-Nielsen ($\exists n_i$ with $6 \mid n_i$ or $2 \mid n_i$) + Balister (no odd squarefree covering) + LCM constraint ($9 \mid \text{lcm}$ or $15 \mid \text{lcm}$).

conclusion.summary: We formalize Erdős Problem #7 (Erdős-Selfridge Conjecture), an OPEN problem asking whether there exists a covering system with all moduli odd. The conjecture predicts NO such system exists. Significant partial results are formalized: Hough-Nielsen (2019) proved some modulus must be divisible by 2 or 3, and Balister et al. (2022) ruled out odd squarefree coverings.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: This problem constrains the structure of covering systems.

If proven, it would show that the prime 2 plays a special role in coverings. The partial results already severely limit what an odd covering could look like: it must have non-squarefree moduli, the LCM must be divisible by 9 or 15, and some modulus must be divisible by 3.
openQuestions: Does an odd covering system exist? (The main question)
If an odd covering exists, what is its minimum number of classes?
What is the structure of the smallest odd covering (if any)?
Can computational searches help resolve this problem?

crossReferences.description: Problem #2 asked whether the minimum modulus of a covering system can be arbitrarily large (answered NO by Hough 2015). Problem #7 is the natural companion: must every covering system include an even modulus? Both constrain the fundamental structure of covering systems
Problem #8 asks about monochromatic covering systems, adding coloring constraints to the covering framework. Problems #2, #7, and #8 form a trio of structural questions about covering systems
Problem #27 on almost covering systems relaxes the coverage requirement. Understanding the parity constraints of Problem #7 informs what near-coverings with odd moduli might look like
The Chinese Remainder Theorem governs how congruence classes with coprime moduli interact, which is essential for constructing or ruling out covering systems with constrained moduli
